# General-H readout, finite quantum criteria and a SciCode2 issue

## Outcome and remaining gap

This round develops reusable general-H repair and evaluation algorithms, proves new endpoint and finite-forward statements, and constructs an English standalone [research issue](../../problem/ISSUE-general-h-finite-annealing.md). The issue passes the local creation screen as a plausible research question. It is not yet a calibrated or organizer-approved benchmark.

The strongest practical advance is cheap matrix/physical-program evaluation without a decoding oracle. It includes a weighted GF2 repair witness, an exact balanced thermal compiler, sparse quantum T²/T⁴ readout moments, and a local-observable finite-T remainder. On ordinary saved candidate pools, moment-guided selection produces9 smaller embeddings out of24, averaging2.73% fewer physical qubits across all24. Those particular finite-T predictions are heuristics, not proved decoding improvements.

The main unresolved question remains a useful, inexpensive theory criterion that orders ACTUAL ORIGINAL-ERROR optimum probability under a finite quantum anneal and guides compact mappings on ordinary generalH. Endpoint certificates, conditional mean-cost improvements and unconditional local-cost orderings each establish different facts. None may silently replace that target.

## Authorization, conditions and experimental discipline

The user allocated three hours beginning2026-10-16T08:57:05Z, ending11:57:05Z, and requested continued research plus an English SciCode2 issue. This is continuing author-context research with an existing scientific child and parent collaboration; neither a fresh autonomous model trial nor calibration. No QPU, paid API, external issue publication or automation was used. Original TASK.md/prompt.md and prior labs remain unchanged, with dependency hashes checked at closeout.

The scientific child independently chose thermal entropy/readout analysis, a balanced compiler and local classical dynamics. The parent developed weighted repair penalties, independent audits and full quantum-forward criteria. Subsequent exchanged ideas/proof reviews are documented collaboration, not human expert interventions. Development/held-out labels apply only to the originally frozen child main protocol; later parent extensions reuse data exploratorily and do not inherit a held-out claim.

Frozen/adaptive protocols: [main](PROTOCOL.md), [parent repair penalty](independent/PENALTY_PROTOCOL.md), [full forward](independent/FORWARD_PROTOCOL.md), [sparse moments](independent/FOURTH_ORDER_PROTOCOL.md), [mapping selection](independent/MOMENT_SELECTION_PROTOCOL.md), [local remainder](independent/LOCAL_FORWARD_PROTOCOL.md), [longer forward](independent/LONG_FORWARD_PROTOCOL.md). Failures, unsuccessful bounds and integration levels are retained. The original budget was never restarted.

## General-H repair algorithm and reduced penalties

[independent/penalty_bound.py](independent/penalty_bound.py) accepts arbitrary binary sparse rows, feasible syndrome and finite signed weights. It greedily finds a minimum-total-|w| column basis B, chooses independent original rows R and computes the GF2 inverse H[R,B]^(−1). A saved exact reconstruction identity verifies that this is a right inverse on imH. Its repair columns Delta_j have loads L_j=Σ_{i in Delta_j}|w_i|. Any syndrome residual repairs at objective-cost increase at mostΣ_j L_j v_j≤C|v|, C=max_jL_j≤Σ_{i inB}|w_i|≤Σ_i|w_i|.

Therefore M>C suffices for the unchanged parity compiler's projected ground fidelity; the study uses M=C+1 and recomputes the rational coefficient gap and actual physical rounding certificate. This is not classical minimum-weight decoding. It works with dependent rows, irregular/higher-order columns, zero/signed weights and all feasible syndromes. The algorithm's costs are bitset Gaussian elimination and output-size dependent; no claim of linear-time elimination follows from sparsity alone.

[Validation](results/penalty_checks.json) covers120 small matrices,6,650 original-error repairs,108 full-QUBO ground enumerations and40 independent minimum-column-basis checks. In the [48-input study](results/penalty_summary.json),36 historical inputs and12 fresh seed8809 inputs use identical mappings per penalty comparison. Mean logical-scale gains are6.02× and6.51× respectively, with median witness calculation about1ms. There is no qubit reduction from this programming-only intervention.

For the16 n16 inputs, outward endpoint intervals prove13 strict ORIGINAL-ERROR optimum probability improvements(10/12 historical,3/4 fresh), zero strict reversals and3 inconclusive comparisons. Auxiliary excitations count as successful when the roots give an optimal feasible correction. These are terminal-Gibbs statements; larger alpha alone is not a decoding-probability ordering across different penalties.

## Balanced compiler and inexpensive endpoint readout evaluation

[Child theory](THEORY.md) and [report](RESEARCH_REPORT.md) prove that four even-flipped independent-hidden XOR factors at strengthM/4 have actual interaction graphK3,4, valid partition factora=(1+r)^4 and invalid factorb=8r(1+r²), r=exp(−beta alpha M). Row-prefix transfer gives exact soft-parity factors. Conditioned on H e=s, the original-error marginal is exactly the intended additive-cost Gibbs law, including all excited auxiliaries. The ordinary compiler can have auxiliary free-energy bias within the feasible set.

A GF2 repair bijection gives a cheap syndrome feasibility bound and, with chain/rounding/entropy terms, an original-error distribution TV certificate. Balanced post-witness evaluation is linear in row/output size. The ordinary row-envelope audit can costO(Σd2^d); it explicitly returns inconclusive above degree20. Measured balanced witness+readout evaluation is median0.98ms, versus3.84ms ordinary, with ordinary worst case343ms at degree17.

The main study has24 new ordinary matrices: four unrelated sparse generators, n16/32/64, seeds8807(development) and9901(reserved). Standard fits24/24; balanced fits23/24 within the same eight-seed search budget. The balanced failure is a heuristic search failure, not proved impossibility. On23 common inputs it uses1.998× physical qubits and1.806× logical scale. It improves beta20 TV≤.25 coverage from8/23 to16/23, but is not a compact representation win.

Independent [positive interval transfer](results/independent_readout_intervals.json) checks64 actual n16 programs. Strict balanced root-decoded-optimum endpoint orders are3/8 at beta10,6/8 at20,8/8 at40 and8/8 at80, with no strict reverse. The balanced transfer is independently checked by a70-digit full256-state physical sum. Separately, [373 saved-program audits](results/independent_child_program_audit.json)(309 distinct core witnesses) check rational reduction fidelity, physical ranges, chain margins and outward rounding/defect terms. These program sets differ from the child's188 beta-curve audits; their maxima must not be pooled as one audit.

## A rigorous dynamics warning and finite classical evidence

The child proves a random-scan local heat-bath/Metropolis mixing obstruction: a physical original-root flip must cross a broken-branch endpoint. Reversibility bounds indicator conductance by branch-defect probability divided by the number of physical spins. A general-H kernel witness bounds the root marginal away from0 and1; a spectral/mixing lower bound follows. This concerns a terminal CLASSICAL hold, not coherent quantum dynamics, typical-start decoding time or optimum failure probability.

The strongest beta20 example uses a nonzero-cost kernel pair[14,41], cost1.75, and yields a1.68e15-sweep worst-case mixing lower bound. Certified chain relaxation reduces that bound to660 sweeps while preserving the requested consistency budget. A smaller obstruction bound does not prove faster actual mixing.

Finite-work classical anneals provide an important negative result. Under matched attempted physical-site-update budgets, mean n16 optimum success is0.00757 ordinary versus0.00195 balanced; their terminal references are0.04352 and0.12039. The compiler ordering reverses. Equal attempts mean different sweeps when physical sizes differ, which is explicitly charged. All109,824 saved physical outputs pass independent rescoring. n32 exact optima yield0/4096 at the largest budget; n64 optimum success is unassessed, rather than called failure. These are CLASSICAL results and cannot establish quantum ordering.

## Actual full quantum-forward theory and anchors

The parent uses the complete physical closed-system schedule K(u)=−(1−u)ΣX+uE(Z), initial|+> on EVERY active spin, durationT, and declared root readout. All auxiliary/branch excitations are included in the original-error success event. Fields/couplers are actual programmed coefficients. This is a defined research model, not a validated commercial-device noise model.

[FORWARD_THEORY.md](independent/FORWARD_THEORY.md) proves the relative T² original-optimum coefficient under fixed-coupler objective amplification is Delta_eta(Σw−2C*)/12. Affine feasible-cost moments give a cheap optimum upper bound without solving decoding. An exact-rational global Dyson remainder plus actual field-rounding correction proves strict finite-forward optimum orders on45/48 ordinary pairs. The3 inconclusive cases are retained. Certified durations are only1.19e−7 to3.05e−5(median3.81e−6); their effects are operationally tiny. This is a genuine finite-QA theorem, but not a practical closure.

[Sixteen full physical anchors](results/forward_anchor_summary.json), four matrix generators at n6/n8 and two seeds, use9–18 physical spins. At all five durations(.05,.25,1,4,16), amplified programs numerically improve the actual original-optimum probability on16/16. AtT16 cohort mean success changes0.10355→0.19460. All160 program-duration runs converge by step doubling. A separate adaptive DOP853 [40-case audit](results/forward_ode_audit.json) agrees with the independent Strang backend within2.50e−6 in optimum probability. These tractable general-H anchors are validation, not large-instance proofs.

The [longer-duration extension](results/long_forward_summary.json) retains all eight original n6 anchors atT32/64/128, both programs, with separate budget/convergence limits. Its final outcome is recorded at closeout.

## Sparse quantum moments and compact mapping decisions

[QUANTUM_MOMENT_THEORY.md](independent/QUANTUM_MOMENT_THEORY.md) derives q2=LE/12 and the linked log-probability q4=−L³E/1344+LB/2240+C/576−D/1344. For pairwise physical interactions these are sparse local-star Walsh polynomials. GF2 kernel characters compute feasible probability and conditional feasible mean-cost coefficients without enumerating errors or physical states. Arithmetic operation count isO(N+|J|+Σdegree³+nP), plus elimination; the implementation's wide integer masks carry additional bit costs.

Fixed-coupler objective amplification changes the conditional mean-cost T² coefficient by−Delta_eta Var_F(cost)/6≤0, valid for generalH and signed weights. This is a quantum coefficient identity, not a Gibbs statement or an unconditional optimum ordering. [Exact independent Dyson checks](results/fourth_order_checks.json) pass24 arbitrary physical models/278 basis states. [143-program evaluation](results/quantum_moment_summary.json) takes median10–14ms, maximum118ms. Independent ODE anchors retain the failure of truncated predictions at longer durations.

The [compact selection study](results/moment_selection_summary.json) reconstructs all192 programs from the24 saved eight-candidate STANDARD pools. AtT=.25 it keeps only candidates with no more qubits than the first automatic candidate and nonworse T^4-predicted feasibility/conditional cost. Ten selections change;9 strictly reduce qubits; mean reduction is2.73% across all24. Median moment calculation is9.96ms; all candidate reconstruction/selection takes10.87s. There is no extra minor search or decoding solve. The comparison is against FIRST candidate, not the prior compactness/alpha-selected mapping. Because no useful T^4 transfer remainder is supplied for these joint events, this is an implemented exploratory heuristic with theoretical coefficients, not proved finite-time decoding gain.

## Local-observable finite-T remainder

[LOCAL_FORWARD_THEORY.md](independent/LOCAL_FORWARD_THEORY.md) proves a bound from termwise nested commutators, support growth and local incident strength gE=max_q(|h_q|+Σ|J_qr|). A support-s diagonal observable's remainder beyondT^4 is bounded by the even negative-binomial tail atx=(1+gE)|T|<1. For a single-root observable the tail isx^6/(1−x²), independent of total physical spin count.

Using exact rational coefficients of the actual binary64 programs, this certifies UNCONDITIONAL original-error MEAN-COST improvements on48/48 ordinary pairs at menu durations.0125 or.025(median.025), median174ms evaluation. Independent adaptive ODE checks pass24 anchor program/time combinations. This greatly improves the time regime for a local observable; it does not certify syndrome feasibility or minimum-cost feasible-error probability. A low mean cost may come from invalid corrections. The unresolved global decoding event must not be replaced by this result.

## Issue, requirements assessment and evidence status

The standalone English [issue](../../problem/ISSUE-general-h-finite-annealing.md) and [PDF](../../problem/issue-general-h-finite-annealing.pdf) state generalH,s,w, hardware input, the full finite quantum schedule, primary original-error success event, open algorithmic choices and independently checkable claims. Only public references are required. No private proposal, research answer or old conversation is an input.

The [author-only assessment](../../evaluation/ISSUE-ASSESSMENT-general-h-finite-annealing.md) recommends **pass-to-testing**, with useful-regime feasibility and difficulty still uncertain. The old broad problem allowed a conditional result and was provisionally solved in Lab002; that success is preserved. This continuation cannot become evidence of fresh-agent failure, formal A/B calibration, human expert intervention or organizer approval. The complete linked organizer template remains inaccessible; no guarantee of acceptance is claimed. A trial-specific input/protocol manifest is later execution preparation, not a gate for this creation-stage issue.

Canonical sources remain in this lab. [Child report](RESEARCH_REPORT.md), [theory](THEORY.md), [environment](results/research_environment.json), protocol files, actual coefficient/embedding witnesses, integration levels and classical outputs support the claims above. Parent independent code is underindependent/; scripts/ is the child's study. Only reference scoring enumerates optimal original errors or full quantum states. Construction/selection does not consume those answers.

At closeout, verify source hashes/manifests, preserve this round's exact root/child transcript lines with source line maps, update run.json and ingest only supported claims into the benchmark wiki. Strengthen the thesis with general-H repair/readout and finite-quantum primitives; retain the practical finite-time decoding gap, classical ordering reversal, balanced resource overhead, heuristic compact selection and calibration uncertainty. Do not promote proxy improvements into actual success guarantees.

Checked16 October2026. The following sources provide context, not priority evidence for the independently derived local implementation.

[Gyhm et al., Boltzmann Sampling by Diabatic Quantum Annealing, arXiv2409.18126v4](https://arxiv.org/html/2409.18126v4), SecsII/IV, derives a weak-coupling interaction-picture approximation with different response factors for fields and pair interactions. Its illustrative linear quench differs from this lab's fixed normalized forward schedule. It supports treating a Gibbs interpretation as a regime-dependent approximation, not an identity. Our finite-T expansion, affine-cost bound and explicit remainder are derived and checked locally; no novelty claim is made for Dyson/short-time reasoning.

[Amin, Searching for quantum speedup in quasistatic quantum annealers](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.04216) distinguishes a quasistatic frozen population from information about the underlying dynamics. Our terminal-equilibrium theorems do not establish equilibration or quantum speedup.

[Könz et al., Embedding Overhead Scaling of Optimization Problems in Quantum Annealing](https://doi.org/10.1103/PRXQuantum.2.040322) studies space/time overhead with simulated quantum annealing and fully connected source problems. ## Required pages

- `index.md`: top-level local research map that indexes the synthesis and ideas families.
- `thesis.md`: current synthesis, strongest support, contradictions, alternatives, and open questions.
- `ideas/`: hypothesis, frontier, branching, pruning, and distillation pages. These replace `ideas.yml`; preserve IDs and history in the page content.
- `log.md`: append-only operational history.
- `sources.yml`: provenance ledger for ingested raw materials. It stores paths, revisions, ingest times, and affected wiki pages; it never copies or summarizes source content.
- `concepts/`, `methods/`, `implementations/`, `comparisons/`, and `questions/`: compiled pages created when warranted by the material, not one page per heading, source file, or code module by default.

## Page conventions

Use lowercase kebab-case filenames and YAML frontmatter with `title`, `page_type`, `status`, `updated`, `source_refs`, and `idea_ids`. Below the title, every compiled page visibly includes `**Summary**`, `**Sources**`, and `**Last updated**`, and ends with `## Related pages`.

- `$wiki-ingest` previews takeaways and planned changes, then integrates raw sources and updates affected pages, index, thesis, and log. It pauses for materially ambiguous categorization or interpretation.

# Wiki Lint

Check both what can be validated mechanically and what requires scientific judgment. Lint reports problems; it does not erase disagreements to make the wiki look consistent.

## Workflow

1. Read `wiki/SCHEMA.md` and [references/lint-rules.md](references/lint-rules.md).
2. Run:

   ```bash
   python3 skills/wiki-lint/scripts/lint_wiki.py <project-root-or-benchmark-directory>
   ```

   Add `--semantic` for the optional OpenAI-backed knowledge-health review. This mode loads
   `OPENAI_API_KEY` from the project `.env`, uses `OPENAI_SEMANTIC_LINT_MODEL` (falling back
   to `OPENAI_MODEL` and then `gpt-5.6-luna`), and caches strict structured results under
   `.tmp/`. Use `--semantic-limit N` for a bounded smoke test and `--semantic-refresh` only
   when the same evidence should be reviewed again intentionally.

3. Review structural findings: required files, page-format fields, broken or ambiguous Markdown/Obsidian links, including claim citations in the portable `[readable label](relative-path#locator)` form, missing indexed pages, orphan compiled pages, duplicate titles, malformed `sources.yml` entries, and malformed log entries. Reject citation syntaxes that require a source-ID resolver, including backticked or bare `global:...`, `benchmark:...`, and `source:...` IDs outside fenced code examples. For benchmark scope, also check unregistered raw inputs and completed labs. For global scope, check that sources resolve outside `wiki/` and project summaries link to the resources that own their details.
4. Audit semantic health: unsupported claims, contradictions hidden by overwrites, stale thesis statements, concepts mentioned repeatedly without pages, missing inverse links where useful, registered sources that did not change durable synthesis, and high-value gaps. The semantic mode supplies bounded page, neighbor-summary, and provenance packets to the model. Treat every finding as a review candidate rather than established fact.
5. Classify each finding as error, warning, or research opportunity. Cite exact paths. Route findings requiring scientific judgment, ambiguous merges, or prioritization to `$consult-human` as individual threads.

## Fix boundary

Automatically fix only clearly mechanical problems when the user asks: index omissions, link spelling, formatting, or missing reciprocal navigation. Do not automatically resolve scientific contradictions, merge concept pages with distinct meanings, change confidence, or rewrite the thesis. Route substantive corrections through `$wiki-ingest` with source evidence.

## Completion

Report structural status, knowledge-health findings, source coverage, and the highest-value maintenance or research actions as a numbered list with suggested fixes. A zero-error structural result does not imply that the wiki is scientifically complete.

Semantic findings do not change the command exit status and never modify the wiki. API or configuration failures do return a distinct failure because an explicitly requested review did not complete. Token usage is appended to `.tmp/llm-usage.jsonl` without credentials or source text.

# General-H evaluation-guided embedding implementation

**Summary**: An exploratory reusable sparse-input constructor combines the inherited faithful XOR model with tree-load thermal evaluation, automatic candidate selection and optional fixed-tree LP contact allocation.

**Sources**: [Lab 004 report](../../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/REPORT.md), [constructor](../../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/scripts/construct.py), [theory](../../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/THEORY.md).

**Last updated**: 2026-10-16.

## Interface and ownership

Input JSON contains n, sparse rows, syndrome and weights; custom targets require explicit coupling groups, with ranges optionally declared. Output contains the compiled model, target, branches/trees/roots, actual physical coefficients, margins, numeric fidelity audit and a success or failure/inconclusive status. Construction consumes no code-family metadata, hidden error witness or decoding optimum. The compiler/adapter are imported read-only from Lab 002 with saved hashes. [Interface](../../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/scripts/construct.py), [source provenance](../../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/results/source_provenance.json).

## Evaluation and cost

Rooted branch-tree external loads give repair margins and a product Gibbs defect bound without a decoding solve. Uniform contact splitting reduces scale maximization to affine interval intersection. A sparse LP optimizes same-sign contacts/chain strengths for fixed trees/roots; numerical feasible outputs receive exact-rational audits, without exact LP-optimality or globally optimal embedding claims. Current main evaluation median is 18.6 ms, scanning cached target groups. Generic eight-seed heuristic search and final exact audits are additional costs; no universal polynomial search bound exists. [Mathematics/costs](../../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/THEORY.md).

## Coverage and limitations

Ordinary main inputs cover four sparse generators and n=16,32,64; selection is matched on common candidate pools. Uniform guided/pruned average physical-qubit reduction is 6.57%; a later LP/pruning combination gives 5.53% on eight new inputs. The main target is ideal Zephyr g=6,t=4 with illustrative parameter limits. Synthetic defects pass, but all tested n=256 searches fail. This is not a live Advantage2 device profile or all-sparse-H fit guarantee. [Results and retained failures](../../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/REPORT.md).

Independent code validates 313 selected actual programs, including defective graphs and LP refinements. Interval probability comparisons refer to chain-consistent full-QUBO-ground readout; root-decoded optimum comparisons remain inconclusive. Terminal equilibrium and small-driver corrections do not prove finite-time annealing performance. [Independent coefficient audit](../../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/results/independent_program_audit.json), [interval results](../../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/results/independent_logical_gibbs_intervals.json).

[Thesis](../thesis.md); [frontier](../ideas/research-frontier.md); [stable takeaway](../../note/general-h-tree-gibbs.md); [source entry points](../../src/README.md).

# Current thesis and evidence boundary

**Summary**: A family-independent sparse-H compiler, terminal-Gibbs repair certificate and evaluation-guided programming/search loop are implemented and useful on diverse ordinary inputs. This establishes a conditional endpoint result, not general finite-time annealing superiority.

**Sources**: [Lab 002](../labs/lab-002-agent-test-general-h/REPORT.md), [Lab 003](../labs/lab-003-surface-code-encoding-comparison/REPORT.md), [Lab 004](../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/REPORT.md).

**Last updated**: 2026-10-16.

## Central question

Develop an efficient algorithm from a general sparse binary check matrix, syndrome and additive weights to a faithful quadratic model and hardware-valid annealing embedding, coupled to an inexpensive theoretically justified quality evaluation. CSS form, named codes and planar structure are not prerequisites. The [original task](../problem/TASK.md) remains unchanged.

## Supported progression

Lab 002 supplies an exact/rounding-certified XOR compiler and general Zephyr construction, but its compactness is poor against automatic embedding and all 25 ordinary pause certificates are inconclusive. Its strict quantum comparison uses a narrow initial-state/pause regime and admits a preference reversal. [Lab 002 findings](../labs/lab-002-agent-test-general-h/REPORT.md#findings-and-limits).

Lab 003 favors stabilizer/dual variables for the tested ideal-measurement planar surface codes, with better resources up to distance 9 and numerical tiny-system forward-QA evidence. The geometry-specific encoding and penalty proof do not transfer unchanged to arbitrary H. [Lab 003 scope and limits](../labs/lab-003-surface-code-encoding-comparison/REPORT.md#advantages-of-a-and-limits).

Lab 004 proves a rooted-tree repair/terminal-Gibbs defect certificate without decoding or a partition function. Its effective scale guides compact mapping selection and fixed-tree contact allocation. On 36 ordinary sparse inputs, the uniform guided/pruned rule reduces physical qubits on 33/36, mean 6.57%, retaining reference scale and <5% classical equilibrium defect bounds. An adaptively developed LP/pruning rule improves 7/8 entirely new inputs, mean 5.53%. Independent actual-coefficient audits pass 313 saved selected programs. [Lab 004 outcomes](../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/REPORT.md#ordinary-instance-evidence), [independent audit](../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/results/independent_program_audit.json).

## Strongest comparison and its boundary

At fixed compiled model and beta, increasing alpha increases conditional full-QUBO ground probability. Separated intervals prove strict chain-consistent full-QUBO-ground readout improvement on 8/12 ordinary n=16 inputs for uniform-guided-pruned, and 11/12 for LP-selected. They prove no strict unconditional original-error-optimal order on those inputs. Auxiliary excitations distinguish these events. [Independent interval evidence](../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/results/independent_logical_gibbs_intervals.json).

A local transverse-driver correction yields a small-driver quantum **equilibrium** consistency bound. There is no equilibration, mixing-time or finite-time QA theorem. Identical defect certificates can accompany opposite changes in actual chain failures and decoded success; refinement quality constraints also have null effects in the sampled pruning trajectories. [Theory and limitations](../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/THEORY.md), [physical counterexample](../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/results/physical_gibbs_validation.json).

## Remaining research gaps

Finite-time annealing relevance, real-device parameter/precision/noise validation, original-error or logical-observable success guarantees, large-instance routing coverage and general window-change latency remain unresolved. n=128 fits only 3/4 tested generators on the fixed target; all four n=256 searches fail their budgets. Fixed-H syndrome/weight reuse is demonstrated; arbitrary H changes are not. [Extension and updates](../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/REPORT.md#scaling-updates-and-retained-failures).

## Benchmark interpretation

Scientific evidence strengthens achievable conditional-regime solutions. It does not establish model difficulty, expert approval or organizer acceptance. Lab 002 is an exploratory solve; Labs 003/004 use continuing author context and scientific supervision. The old design-only/no-lab-result status in the append-only log is historical, now superseded by completed lab evidence. No earlier scientific report is rewritten or retroactively regraded.

## Related pages

[Index](index.md); [frontier](ideas/research-frontier.md); [implementation](implementations/general-h-embedding-loop.md).

## Scope and outcome

This extension preserves the actual event F: the original roots decode to a
minimum-cost feasible error, counting all ties and allowing arbitrary compiler
auxiliary and branch excitations. It gives a rare-event-relative remainder for
ANY original-root event, then an inexpensive sufficient comparison for matched
objective amplification. It does not replace decoding success by expected cost.

The physical model remains K(u)=−(1−u)Σ_q X_q+uE(Z), u in [0,1], dimensionless
duration T, initial |+> on every active physical spin, and final computational
root readout. E has actual programmed one-site fields and pair couplers. Offsets
commute and are omitted. Arbitrary sparse binary H, dependent rows, finite signed
weights, feasible syndromes and tied optima are allowed. This is not a thermal
model, QPU estimate, adiabatic theorem or comparison between arbitrary mappings.

## 1. A uniform-diagonal norm that retains rare-event mass

Every operator on N physical spins has a unique displacement representation

    A = Σ_v f_v(Z) X^v,
    A[z,z xor v] = f_v(z).

Define the norm

    ||A||_U = Σ_v 2^(−N) Σ_z |f_v(z)|.

Triangle inequality follows componentwise. It is not asserted to be an operator
norm or invariant under arbitrary unitaries. The only properties needed are:

1. |<+|A|+>| ≤ ||A||_U, because X^v|+>=|+>.
2. Translations f(z)→f(z xor q) preserve its uniform L1 norm.
3. Multiplication by a diagonal Pauli character preserves that norm.

For a diagonal event projector P_F supported on n original roots,
||P_F||_U=P0=|F|/2^n. The ratio uses root patterns, not full physical ground states.
P0 is positive when a finite-cost feasible optimum exists; it need not be known
or computed by the evaluator.

For a single Hamiltonian Pauli term cP, each commutator obeys

    ||[cP,f(Z)X^v]||_U ≤ 2|c| E_uniform|f|.

For P=X_q this is the translated difference f(z xor q)−f(z). For diagonal
P=Z_a or Z_a Z_b, it is f(z)[P(z)−P(z xor v)]X^v. These elementary formulas prove
the bound directly, without an invalid multiplication/operator-norm argument.

## 2. Support-relative time-ordered remainder

Track EACH LOCAL-TERM BRANCH before summing. Initially f depends on the n roots
and v=0. A nonzero next local term must touch the current operator support; a
pair term adds at most one physical site. After j commutators its support is at
most n+j. Merging all terms first would destroy this support bound and is not
part of the proof.

Let gE=max_q(|h_q|+Σ_r|J_qr|), and g(u)=1−u+u gE. Summing incident Pauli-term
norms over a support S is at most |S|g(u); internal-edge double counting is
conservative. Hence the norm sum of order-k nested terms is at most

    P0 2^k (n)_k Π_j g(u_j),
    (n)_k=n(n+1)...(n+k−1).

The ordered-simplex integral of the positive symmetric scalar product is
(∫g)^k/k!. Therefore the absolute kth coefficient of Pr_T(F)/P0 is at most

    binom(n+k−1,k) (1+gE)^k.

For real K, real |+><+| and real diagonal P_F, U(−T)=conj U(T), so Pr_T(F) is
even. This remains true under time ordering; conjugation reverses no product.
For x=(1+gE)|T|<1, the relative remainder after T² is bounded by

    R_n,2(x)=[(1−x)^(−n)+(1+x)^(−n)]/2
                 −1−binom(n+1,2)x².

The denominator P0 cancels exactly. An operator-norm observable bound divided by
P0 would lose this property and be useless for rare decoding events. The present
bound depends on original readout support n rather than total N, but it is still
not size independent.

## 3. Sharper driver/diagonal word counts

The special form of K yields stronger low-order majorants. In a local-term
branch after d driver and m diagonal-energy commutators:

- |v|≤d, because only a driver term changes the flip displacement.
- f depends on at most n+m sites. A nonzero diagonal pair term touches v, hence
  an existing support site, and adds at most one new dependence site.
- A driver commutator is nonzero only where f depends on that site. Its total
  norm multiplier is at most 2(n+m)(1−u).
- A diagonal commutator only uses terms incident on v, so its multiplier is at
  most 2d gE u, rather than the whole functional support.

These are termwise counts, not support claims for a sum. Let B[d,m](u) majorize
the norm of all inner-later words at times in [u,1], divided by P0. Set B[0,0]=1
and out-of-range indices zero. Then

    B[d,m](u)=∫_u^1 {
       2(n+m)(1−v) B[d−1,m](v)
       +2d gE v B[d,m−1](v)} dv.

In the Heisenberg Dyson series, the inner Hamiltonians are later in time and
outer ones earlier. Thus the [u,1] orientation is essential. All integrands have
nonnegative scalar majorants. The implementation factors out gE^m and integrates
exact rational polynomials.

Any outermost driver commutator has zero |+> expectation, since each X_q has |+>
as an eigenstate. Only words with an outer diagonal term need remain. Their
relative kth expectation coefficient is bounded by

    C_k(n,gE)=Σ_{d+m=k,m≥1} ∫_0^1 2d gE u B[d,m−1](u) du.

The first inner term must be a driver; the factor d already makes the all-E
words zero. In particular,

    C_2 = n gE/6,
    C_4 = n³ gE/56 + n(35n+17)gE²/1260 + n gE³/168.

For comparison, the generic fourth-order bound scales as n^4(1+gE)^4. The mixed
word bound retains the distinction between energy and driver insertions.
It does not exploit every cancellation or connected-cluster identity.

Fix K=12 before evaluating outcomes. The refined relative remainder is

    R_word(T) = Σ_{k=4,6,...,12}
        min[C_k T^k, binom(n+k−1,k)x^k]
       +{[(1−x)^(−n)+(1+x)^(−n)]/2
           −Σ_{k=0,2,...,12} binom(n+k−1,k)x^k}.

All coefficients inside the final braces are nonnegative. Exact rational
arithmetic avoids subtractive rounding in this tail. Higher orders use the
proved generic bound; no unproved mixed-word infinite-series convergence is
assumed. The two-program remainder is the sum of their separate remainders.

## 4. Actual rounded objective-amplification comparison

The matched programs have identical active sites, roots, driver, couplers and
nonobjective fields. Their actual root-field difference is

    delta h_i = Δη w_i/2 + epsilon_i,
    Δη>0, rho=Σ_i|epsilon_i|,

all interpreted as exact rationals for the saved binary64 values. The known
second-order density coefficient is q2=LE/12, L=Σ_q[f(z^q)−f(z)]. Consequently,
for the original optimum event,

    delta a2 = Δη(Σ_i w_i−2C*)/12
                    −Σ_i epsilon_i E[Z_i|F]/6
             ≥ Δη D_lower/12−rho/6 = A_actual.

D_lower≤Σw−2C* is obtained from the parent's exact affine mean/variance bound
without solving weighted decoding: C*≤mu−Var/(U−mu), with the constant-cost case
handled separately. This extension reuses that proved input and does not claim
its discovery. All tied optima have the same C*, so their uniform mixture obeys
the same bound.

Unlike a generic Duhamel rounding estimate, rounding here is charged directly
to the exact T² coefficient. All higher coefficients are already bounded for
ACTUAL rounded programs, and their odd coefficients remain zero. No separate
linear-in-T rounding penalty is necessary.

Thus

    [Pr_new(F)−Pr_base(F)]/P0
       ≥ A_actual T²−R_base(T)−R_new(T).

A positive exact rational right side certifies strict actual original-error
optimum probability improvement at that finite duration. The event, P0, C* and
optimal error patterns are never enumerated by the certificate. If A_actual≤0
or the remainder dominates, return inconclusive. A positive guarantee is not
universal over all H/s/w; e.g. forced costly feasible bits can oppose the short
forward bias. Static ground-fidelity and hardware-range audits remain separate
prerequisites for using the programs as decoding implementations.

## 5. Costs and limits

For fixed K=12, scalar polynomial majorants depend only on n and are cached;
program-specific work computes actual local strengths and evaluates exact
rational inequalities on a dyadic menu. There is no Hilbert-space or 2^nullity
enumeration. Bit lengths and rational arithmetic costs are charged; constants
in exact output fractions can be large. Hexadecimal numerator/denominator
strings make the saved exact witnesses portable across JSON integer limits.

This improves conservative finite-time ORIGINAL-OPTIMUM guarantees, rather than
only local mean-cost guarantees. It still covers very early evolution, says
nothing about moderate-time interference or practical annealing success, and
retains system-size dependence through n. An increased certified duration is
not an increased absolute success probability claim: P0 itself can be tiny.

## 6. Corollary for different embeddings

The remainder applies separately to any two physical programs reading the same
original variables, even if N, branch sizes, contact locations and root labels
differ. Initial event mass P0 is the same. After uniform nonroot averaging,

    q2_root(e)=−Σ_i h_root_i Z_i/6
                 −Σ_{i<j} J_root_i,root_j Z_i Z_j/3.

Choose Δη>0 and subtract Δη(Σw−2cost)/12 from the difference of these root-only
polynomials. Restrict the residual Q to the affine feasible set. Its GF2 Walsh
constant minus the L1 norm of its nonconstant coefficients gives a pointwise
lower bound L_Q on every feasible error. Then

    delta a2_on_optimum ≥ Δη D_lower/12+L_Q.

Together with separate event-relative tails, this is a sufficient actual
optimum-event comparison across mappings without an optimum oracle. All source
fidelity/range/graph checks remain necessary. For the balanced compiler with
row degrees at least three, no source original-original couplings remain and
original-root fields contain only the objective; with root-local field
programming this reduces to logical alpha differences plus actual rounding.
Degree-one/two rows require retaining their root-only parity terms explicitly.

This corollary is not evaluated/promoted in the present extension. It identifies
how a certified early-time mapping loop could be implemented; it does not assert
ordinary-instance compactness gains or useful moderate-time comparisons.

## Appendix: explicit fourth-order word integrals

Write D/E words in inner-to-outer order. Only D-D-D-E, D-D-E-E, D-E-D-E and
D-E-E-E contribute to the majorant. Their ordered schedule integrals are,
respectively, 1/2688, 1/4480, 17/40320 and 1/2688. Their norm factors are
48n³gE, 64n²gE², 32n(n+1)gE² and 16ngE³. Multiplying and summing gives the stated
C4 exactly. These scalar integrals integrate the actual factors (1−u) for D and
u for E in the outer-earlier simplex; no unordered-word factorial is inserted.

# A computable original-optimum quantum certificate across embeddings

## Event and assumptions

Use the exact full physical forward model and original-root readout defined in the report. The event F is e_out∈S*, the minimum-cost FEASIBLE original-error set, including ties. Every other physical spin is unobserved; excited auxiliaries and broken branches are included whenever the roots decode correctly. Two programs may have different physical size, couplers, roots or embeddings. Their uniform initial event mass P0=|S*|/2^n is identical. It is not computed during selection.

The [relative-event theorem](../theory_extensions/THEORY.md) bounds each program's normalized event probability remainder using a translation-invariant uniform-diagonal L1 norm. It retains P0, so no rare-event division is lost. The schedule-aware driver/energy word recurrence bounds even orders6..12; the proved generic local-support tail bounds higher orders. This work adds physical-program-specific T²/T⁴ event coefficients and a low-cost mapping decision.

## Exact projected fourth coefficient without finding S*

For each actual program, calculate exact rational q2 and log-probability q4. The fourth density coefficient is p4=q4+q2²/2. An affine parametrization of H e=s maps each original root spin to a signed GF2 kernel character. Each unobserved spin has its independent uniform physical character. Group the q2 polynomial by(unobserved mask, kernel character), yielding polynomials g2_u in the kernel variables; group q4 similarly.

Uniformly averaging ALL unobserved spins leaves

    p4_F = g4_0 + (1/2)Σ_u(g2_u ⋆ g2_u),

where⋆ is XOR convolution of GF2 characters. This is a pointwise polynomial in feasible original errors, not just a feasible average. For candidate-minus-baseline difference δp4_F=b0+Σ_{k≠0}bkχk, define

    L4=b0−Σ_{k≠0}|bk|.

Every feasible error has δp4_F(e)≥L4, hence so does the uniform mixture over the UNKNOWN optimum set. No minimum-weight decoding or optimal-error enumeration is required. Exact grouping must preserve fractions; the earlier floating-point grouped() routine is not used here.

The polynomial construction uses local-star algebra, GF2 elimination and groupwise convolution. Convolution can be quadratic in group size; it is not claimed universally linear. Wide integer character masks and rational bit lengths carry additional costs. On these physical sparse graphs the groups remain modest.

## Cost-constrained second-order lower bound

Likewise δq2_F=a0+Σakχk. Feasible cost is μ+Σckχk and a cheap affine-moment bound supplies C*≤U*. For anyλ≥0 and optimal error,

    δq2_F(e)≥δq2_F(e)+λ(cost(e)−U*)
             ≥a0+λ(μ−U*)−Σ_{k≠0}|ak+λck| = L2(λ).

The first inequality uses cost(e)=C*≤U*. The second bounds each character in[−1,1]. The right side is concave piecewise linear inλ. Its exact maximum is attained at0 or a nonnegative breakpoint−ak/ck. No maximum at infinity is omitted: its final slope isμ−U*−Σ|ck|≤0, because μ−Σ|ck|≤C*≤U*. A zero slope produces a flat tail reached at a finite breakpoint or0. Zero/signed weights, rank deficiency, dependent checks, fixed coordinates and tied optima are allowed.

For pure objective amplification this includesλ=Delta_eta/6 and reproduces the earlier second-order optimum bound. For different embeddings it additionally accounts for actual root-field and root-root-coupler differences. There is no need to pretend that logical scale alone determines q2.

## Finite-time certificate and algorithm

Let L2=maxλL2(λ), and let R_A,>4(T),R_B,>4(T) be the proved separate relative event tails beyondT4. Then

    [Pr_B(F)−Pr_A(F)]/P0
       ≥L2 T²+L4 T⁴−R_A,>4(T)−R_B,>4(T).

A positive exact rational value proves a strict actual original-optimum probability improvement at that common finite duration. It does not estimate the unknown absolute probability or claim a useful effect size. Static fidelity, graph validity and ranges are separate prerequisites.

Given H,s,w and a target/programming specification, compile a faithful model, search a fixed automatic candidate pool, construct actual physical programs, compute the affine witness and coefficient bounds, and select the smallest candidate within the baseline qubit cap whose finite-time comparison is positive. Otherwise return the baseline or inconclusive. Representation and candidate generation are separable from the certificate. The implementation accepts generalH and returns meaningful bounds only where its sufficient conditions permit.

## Independent checks and ordinary-input evidence

[event_projection_checks.py](event_projection_checks.py) independently integrates exact time-polynomial Dyson amplitudes on24 arbitrary small physical program pairs with different physical sizes/root locations. All2,688 basis states,352 projected coefficients and24 adaptive-ODE original-optimum event inequalities pass. Optima are enumerated ONLY for validation; the tested algorithm receives no answer. The child independently reviewed the grouping, convolution, Lagrange sign/breakpoint argument and cross-size event normalization. Explicit D/E-word enumeration independently agrees with all18 tested recurrence coefficients.

For48 fixed-coupler repaired-penalty pairs, the T4-specific event certificate proves45 strict orders, same3 inconclusive cases as the original curvature theorem. Largest certified dyadic duration is.00390625–.03125, median.0078125, median2048× larger than the original global-norm proof and8× larger than the word-only proof. Median evaluation is177ms, maximum766ms. This improves a proved time regime, not measured absolute success.

The mapping study preserves each compiler and its global penaltyM, and uses all375 successful candidates from47 main models:24 standard,23 balanced. One balanced model failed every search and another has seven successful candidates; both failures remain recorded. There is no new minor search or repaired-penalty amplification in this comparison.

At the predeclared primaryT=1/1024, the balanced model has17/23 certified mapping changes,15 strict qubit reductions and mean4.075% qubit reduction across all23. The standard model has0/24 certified changes over the entire declared duration menu. This is inconclusiveness, not proof that no standard mapping is better. The selected balanced relative advantage lower bounds range3.06e−12–6.18e−8, median2.62e−10. For unknownP0 as small as one optimal pattern/2^64, absolute guaranteed gains can be extraordinarily small.

AtT=1/64 there are4/23 balanced certified changes and3 smaller mappings; at1/256 there are14 changes and12 smaller mappings. The full common-duration frontier is retained. Total criterion work on375 candidates is34.67s, median0.608s per eight-search pool; programming adds5.90s, with standard saved reconstructions reused. Total45.32s includes serialization/audits. These are host measurements, not worst-case complexity guarantees.

## What is and is not closed

This establishes a genuine early-time theory-guided COMPACT MAPPING loop for ordinary generalH within the balanced compiler, with actual original-optimum event comparisons. It is stronger than comparing only equilibrium, mean cost or an unbounded Taylor proxy. It is not a practical general decoding solution: the balanced compiler costs about twice the physical qubits of the standard one, time is very early, bounds are tiny, standard-compiler selection is inconclusive, and no moderate-time/live-device transfer is established. The pools are reused exploratory data, not a new held-out confirmation or difficulty trial.

If a paper folder includes a repository, treat the folder as a bundle and the paper and code snapshot as separate sources with separate revisions and `updated_pages`. Static code inspection supports statements about architecture and interfaces, not runtime correctness or reproduction of paper results. Create a paper-to-code comparison when the implemented objective, level of description, or algorithm differs materially from the paper method a reader might otherwise assume it realizes.

Reusable scientific pages belong globally. When promoting knowledge from a benchmark wiki, move the general synthesis and leave benchmark-specific hypotheses, decisions, implementation constraints, and lab evidence local. Replace duplicate local pages with cross-scope links and append migration records; do not maintain parallel full copies.

## Claims

For consequential claims, preserve:

- the claim and calibrated confidence;
- supporting and challenging raw sources;
- scope and assumptions;
- whether it is source-reported, lab-observed, or wiki synthesis;
- related concepts, methods, comparisons, questions, and ideas.

## Contradictions

Never overwrite an older claim just because a new source disagrees. Record both scoped claims, identify possible reasons for disagreement, update the thesis only to the degree justified, and create an open question when the conflict is unresolved.

## Idempotence

Before ingest, inspect the matching `sources.yml` entry and log. Re-ingesting the same revision should not duplicate pages, links, or log claims. If a source changed, update its revision and affected-page list and explain which compiled conclusions changed.

## Ingest preview

Before mutation, show the human the extracted takeaways, possible contradictions, planned page changes, and proposed thesis effect. Human review is mandatory for ambiguous ontology, conflicting interpretations, or consequential scope changes. A routine ingest may continue after a visible preview when the user already authorized the operation and no material decision remains.

{"chunk_id":"ad6fe8","wall_time_seconds":0.0000225,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":2171,"output":"# Standard-compiler mapping limitation and necessary-optimality extension

The original necessary-optimality relaxation improves many bounds but certifies
no standard-compiler mapping changes. Combining its strongest character
constraints with cheap feasible-cost witnesses proves three compact standard
mapping improvements on n16 inputs; all n32/64 cases remain inconclusive. The
proof concerns actual original-optimum finite-forward probability, not mean cost.
This is a limited constructive result with retained negative controls.

## Protocol and event

All24 saved standard-compiler inputs and their192 successful original automatic
candidates are retained. The compiler/globalM, programmed target/ranges, first
candidate baseline, actual programs, exact T4 polynomial and event tails are
unchanged. The primary duration is T=1/1024; all seven declared durations
1/64,...,1/4096 are reported. No new mapping, physical evolution or ordinary
optimum enumeration is performed.

The scored event is minimum-cost feasible ORIGINAL-error root readout, including
ties and arbitrary branch/auxiliary states. Standard-|+> physical initialization
and K(u)=−(1−u)ΣX+uE(Z) remain explicit. Each comparison is between candidates of
the SAME standard compiler. Baseline is FIRST automatic candidate, seed11 in
all24 pools; gains are not versus the previously compact alpha-guided mapping.

PROTOCOL.md froze cost-only, basis moves, basis+pairs and triangle-augmented
controls before outcomes. UPPER_BOUND_PROTOCOL.md separately froze the negative
curvature diagnostic after no positive certificates. WITNESS_PROTOCOL.md froze
a bounded feasible-cost search; its subsequent addenda record the parent's
zero-search particular-solution control and the required mechanism controls.
This is adaptive continuing research, not a blind/held-out test or difficulty
calibration. No frozen main/word/event/mapping snapshot is modified.

## Theory and implementation

THEORY.md proves necessary kernel-move inequalities, valid three-character
facets, and an exact dual box lower bound for unknown optimal-error characters.
HiGHS only proposes nonnegative multipliers. Exact Fraction evaluation charges
all residual coefficients and does not rely on numerical LP optimality or
primal feasibility. Every nonzero multiplier and exact bound is saved.

The affine-cost upper bound U* is first the parent's moment bound. The particular
solution and searched feasible error can tighten U* because C* cannot exceed
ANY feasible cost. Neither is called optimum. The searched witness uses16 fixed
kernel starts and basis/pair best-improving descent capped at4n moves/start.
No planted error or ordinary reference optimum enters construction.

The implementation supports finite signed binary64 weights exactly via Fraction
and an LCM denominator, rather than assuming integer-quarter weights. Ordinary
weights have small dyadic precision; timings do not guarantee similar cost at
arbitrary bit precision. The theoretical inequalities apply to arbitrary finite
signed costs and general binary H with feasible syndrome.

## All ordinary controls and outcomes

Every method retains all24 matrices, every192 candidate and every duration.
The following primary-T outcomes also hold at every declared duration:

| Feasible-cost upper bound | Character constraints | Certified changes /24 | Strict smaller | Mean qubit reduction across24 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Parent moment bound | Cost-only |0|0|0|
| Parent moment bound | Basis moves |0|0|0|
| Parent moment bound | Basis+pairs |0|0|0|
| Parent moment bound | Basis+pairs+triangles |0|0|0|
| Particular cost | Cost-only |0|0|0|
| Particular cost | Basis or basis+pairs |0|0|0|
| Particular cost | Basis+pairs+triangles |1|1|.4032%|
| Searched witness cost | Cost-only |0|0|0|
| Searched witness cost | Basis or basis+pairs |0|0|0|
| Searched witness cost | Basis+pairs+triangles |3|3|.6563%|

The initial triangle relaxation strengthens164/192 moment-based lower bounds by
more than1e-10 (maximum improvement .5207), but none becomes positive. Thus this
negative result is not merely an unchanged calculation. The strongest relaxation
has at most86 variables/732 inequalities. Applying it to minus the difference
polynomial gives no negative upper-curvature certificate, including all94
nonbaseline candidates with N≤FIRST. Neither favorable nor adverse standard
ordering follows from the original moment-only relaxation.

The searched witness tightens U* onall24 inputs, costs median14.0ms,total1.39s,
and evaluates715,220 kernel moves. None of its384 starts hits the accepted-move
cap. The already computed particular solution also tightens U* onall24, with
median.142ms,total5.72ms additional exact-cost/syndrome checks and zero search.
Its proposal was a subsequent parent collaboration, documented before outcomes.

The three positive selected comparisons, all at original n16, are:

| Input | FIRST seed / qubits | Selected seed / qubits | Relative optimum advantage lower at T1/1024 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|mixed_hypergraph_n16_s8807|11 /111|173 /110|4.44e-8|
|rewired_band_n16_s8807|11 /58|211 /55|1.25e-8|
|rewired_band_n16_s9901|11 /62|47 /56|5.56e-8|

The particular-only triangle control obtains the final row. Search adds the
first two. None of the evaluated cost-only/basis/pair controls obtains them,
so stronger upper witnesses alone do not explain the combined certificates.
This does not assert that these constraints are logically necessary for every
possible proof method. All16 standard n32/64 models remain inconclusive.

Positive lower bounds refer to [P_selected(opt)−P_FIRST(opt)]/P0. P0 is unknown
uniform optimum mass and may be small. These are correct early-time conditional
regime results; they neither establish a useful success rate nor a moderate-time
ranking. The larger balanced compiler is not used as a hidden resource subsidy.

## Costs, validation and provenance

Initial24-pool three-method evaluation takes3.76s; numerical LP medians are
approximately1–2ms/candidate. The negative diagnostic takes4.08s. Particular+
strongest-LP and searched-witness+strongest-LP runs take2.52s and3.30s respectively.
Both tightened-upper cost-only controls together take1.99s. The complete nested
controls with particular/search uppers take4.20s/4.19s. These are incremental
costs: parent GF2 preprocessing, automatic embedding, physical programming and
exact q2/q4/tail computations are inherited and not included again. The parent
records those costs separately; this is not a standalone end-to-end timing.

Sixty arbitrary small binary matrices with dependent rows and signed/zero
weights supply independent validation, not ordinary selection. Exact reference
optimum enumeration checks75 tied optimal patterns,2,084 necessary inequalities,
480 exact lower/upper dual bounds, and60 feasible-search witnesses. All pass.
The ordinary selector never enumerates its optimum set. Parent independently
reviewed the kernel inequality sign, triangle facets and exact dual proof.

The root-only q2 extractor is independently checked against all192 saved exact
parent cost-Lagrange values before any bound change. Exact witnesses include
nonzero dual multipliers, source hashes, feasible original-error masks, descent
counts, cost bounds and all duration outcomes. One initial reader mismatch with
the parent's migrated Fraction-hex schema is retained; it occurred before
outcome collection and did not change the scientific criterion.

## Interpretation

This branch provides a modest correct standard-compiler finite-event compact
mapping result, and stronger evidence of the remaining limitation: most ordinary
standard inputs, including all larger tested ones, remain unresolved despite
substantially stronger inexpensive bounds. It does not prove that no useful
standard mapping exists, that true candidate order is adverse, or that the
relaxation is tight. Cheap feasible witnesses are approximate cost searches and
are charged as such. No optimum oracle or special-code assumption closes the gap.

An ANY-conditional-finite-event benchmark cannot dismiss these correct early-time
certificates merely because their regime is conservative. Practical/informative
regime and broad larger-input coverage remain distinct scientific questions.
No model difficulty or organizer acceptance conclusion is inferred here.

A final exact replay, without any LP or optimum solve, verifies1,728 saved dual
certificates,12,096 event-gap updates and all48 ordinary feasible witnesses
(particular plus searched). See results/exact_audit.json. This checks all initial
and tightened-upper nested-control witnesses, including negative outcomes.

{"chunk_id":"a3c255","wall_time_seconds":0.000010416,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":1576,"output":"# Necessary-optimality bounds without an optimum oracle

The physical/event model is unchanged from the parent's certified mapping study:
standard-|+> initialization, K(u)=−(1−u)ΣX+uE(Z), final original-root readout, and
the event of a minimum-cost feasible ORIGINAL error (all ties; arbitrary compiler
and chain excitations). This extension only improves the lower bound on the
actual second-order event coefficient. It does not replace the event by cost.

## General feasible characters

For arbitrary binary H and feasible s, exact GF2 elimination gives

    e(y)=e0 xor Vy,    y in GF2^k.

Write each original spin as Z_i=(2e0_i−1)χ_{a_i}(y), where
χ_a(y)=(−1)^(a·y). Thus the original cost is

    C(y)=mu+Σ_{a≠0} c_a χ_a(y).

Fixed coordinates and signed/zero weights are included in mu and c. Let U* be
ANY proved upper bound on the unknown minimum C*: the parent's affine-moment
bound, the exact cost of e0, or the cost of a verified feasible witness. No
claim that a feasible witness is optimal is necessary or permitted.

For any two actual physical programs read to the same original variables,
uniform nonroot averaging gives the exact second-order difference polynomial

    f(y)=delta q2_F(y)=a0+Σ_{a≠0} a_a χ_a(y).

The root-only coefficients are extracted directly from actual binary64 fields
and root-root couplers as exact Fractions: −h_i Z_i/6 and −J_ij Z_i Z_j/3.
Unobserved branch/auxiliary terms average to zero at this order. Root labels,
branch sizes and total physical spin counts may differ. The final event's
initial mass P0 depends only on original optimal patterns and is the same.

## Necessary optimality inequalities

For any selected nonzero parameter move t, a global optimum obeys
C(y xor t)−C(y)≥0. Character multiplication therefore proves

    Σ_{a:a·t=1} c_a χ_a(y)≤0.

The implementation includes fundamental moves t=unit_j, then all parameter
pairs unit_i xor unit_j. These are polynomially many necessary conditions,
not a global optimization oracle. They apply to every tied optimum, even if a
separate feasible witness is not locally optimal or hits its search cap.

For any nonzero a,b,c=a xor b, characters obey χ_c=χ_aχ_b. The convex hull of
(χ_a,χ_b,χ_c) is described by the four valid inequalities

    −x_a−x_b−x_c≤1,
    −x_a+x_b+x_c≤1,
     x_a−x_b+x_c≤1,
     x_a+x_b−x_c≤1.

Only triples induced by original-coordinate character pairs whose XOR is already
present are included. There is no exponential character closure or claim that
these facets describe all feasible character vectors.

Together with Σc_a x_a≤U*−mu and −1≤x_a≤1, these inequalities define a relaxation
containing every unknown optimal error character vector and any mixture of ties.

## Exact dual lower certificate

Collect the selected necessary inequalities as A x≤b. For ANY nonnegative
multipliers nu, and every actual optimum,

    f(y)≥a0−nu·b−Σ_a |a_a+(nu^T A)_a| = L2(nu).

Indeed f+nu·(Ax−b)≤f, and minimizing the left expression over the box gives the
formula. This proof does not require the numerical LP to be optimal, its primal
solution to be feasible, or any near-zero residual to be ignored.

HiGHS proposes multipliers from the numerical LP's inequality marginals.
Nonnegative binary64 multipliers are converted to exact rational values; negative
proposals are clipped to zero. All remaining coefficients are charged in the
exact L1 box minimum. The saved witness identifies every nonzero multiplier by
constraint ID. Earlier valid bounds are retained by taking their maximum, so a
weak numerical proposal never invalidates a previously proved lower bound.

The parent's one-dimensional cost-only Lagrange bound is a special case. Exact
breakpoint maximization of it is retained as a mechanism control under both
improved upper witnesses.

## Composition with the actual event certificate

The parent's exact physical fourth-order polynomial supplies a pointwise
feasible lower bound L4. The proved relative word-majorant tails bound the
remainder beyond T4 separately for both programs. Hence

    [P_candidate(opt)−P_first(opt)]/P0
      ≥ L2 T²+L4 T⁴−R_candidate,>4−R_first,>4.

The extension reuses the parent's EXACT stored lower gaps and updates them by
(L2_new−L2_old)T². This changes no fourth coefficient, physical program, event,
duration, tail or resource condition. All ordinary decisions use exact rational
positivity. Candidate selection is smallest N≤FIRST among strict certificates,
then greatest exact proved lower gap, then original seed; fallback FIRST.

For an upper bound on actual second-order difference, apply the same relaxation
to −f and negate its lower bound. A nonnegative upper bound is inconclusive.
No adverse actual ordering was proved in this study.

## Feasible witnesses and computational scope

The zero-search witness is the already computed affine particular solution e0.
Its original error is directly checked against H/s and its cost summed exactly.
The searched witness uses 16 fixed feasible kernel starts, then best-improving
fundamental/pair kernel descent, capped at4n accepted moves per start. Every move
stays feasible. The best visited error is a valid cost upper witness regardless
of local termination; it is not asserted optimal. No ordinary reference optimum
or planted generator error is consulted.

The implementation forms exact Fraction values of finite signed binary64 weights
and scales them by the LCM of their denominators. This supports arbitrary finite
binary64 weights, not only quarters. Measured instances have small dyadic
weights; large denominator/numerator bit lengths can substantially increase
integer/rational work. Arbitrary-real exact weights and arbitrary-precision
input formats are not claimed by the JSON interface. LP proposals use floating
arithmetic, but the returned bound is checked algebraically in exact arithmetic.

Basis/pair move enumeration and selected triangle construction are polynomial;
GF2 preprocessing, numerical LP cost and exact bit complexity are not promised
linear in general H. The ordinary suite measures n16/32/64 and bounded target
hardware. Only the small validation suite enumerates optima, explicitly separated
from ordinary construction/selection.

# General-H evaluation-guided embedding implementation

**Summary**: An exploratory reusable sparse-input constructor combines the inherited faithful XOR model with tree-load thermal evaluation, automatic candidate selection and optional fixed-tree LP contact allocation.

**Sources**: [Lab 004 report](../../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/REPORT.md), [constructor](../../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/scripts/construct.py), [theory](../../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/THEORY.md).

**Last updated**: 2026-10-16.

## Interface and ownership

Input JSON contains n, sparse rows, syndrome and weights; custom targets require explicit coupling groups, with ranges optionally declared. Output contains the compiled model, target, branches/trees/roots, actual physical coefficients, margins, numeric fidelity audit and a success or failure/inconclusive status. Construction consumes no code-family metadata, hidden error witness or decoding optimum. The compiler/adapter are imported read-only from Lab 002 with saved hashes. [Interface](../../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/scripts/construct.py), [source provenance](../../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/results/source_provenance.json).

## Evaluation and cost

Rooted branch-tree external loads give repair margins and a product Gibbs defect bound without a decoding solve. Uniform contact splitting reduces scale maximization to affine interval intersection. A sparse LP optimizes same-sign contacts/chain strengths for fixed trees/roots; numerical feasible outputs receive exact-rational audits, without exact LP-optimality or globally optimal embedding claims. Current main evaluation median is 18.6 ms, scanning cached target groups. Generic eight-seed heuristic search and final exact audits are additional costs; no universal polynomial search bound exists. [Mathematics/costs](../../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/THEORY.md).

## Coverage and limitations

Ordinary main inputs cover four sparse generators and n=16,32,64; selection is matched on common candidate pools. Uniform guided/pruned average physical-qubit reduction is 6.57%; a later LP/pruning combination gives 5.53% on eight new inputs. The main target is ideal Zephyr g=6,t=4 with illustrative parameter limits. Synthetic defects pass, but all tested n=256 searches fail. This is not a live Advantage2 device profile or all-sparse-H fit guarantee. [Results and retained failures](../../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/REPORT.md).

Independent code validates 313 selected actual programs, including defective graphs and LP refinements. Interval probability comparisons refer to chain-consistent full-QUBO-ground readout; root-decoded optimum comparisons remain inconclusive. Terminal equilibrium and small-driver corrections do not prove finite-time annealing performance. [Independent coefficient audit](../../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/results/independent_program_audit.json), [interval results](../../labs/lab-004-general-h-evaluation-embedding-loop/results/independent_logical_gibbs_intervals.json).

## Lab005 interfaces and evidence

[Weighted repair witness](../../labs/lab-005-general-h-annealing-relevance/independent/penalty_bound.py) computes exact GF2 repair loads and sufficient parity penalties without weighted decoding. [Sparse quantum moments](../../labs/lab-005-general-h-annealing-relevance/independent/forward_moments.py) and [event selector](../../labs/lab-005-general-h-annealing-relevance/independent/certified_mapping.py) evaluate actual physical readout polynomials/word tails, with explicit inconclusive output. Different physical sizes and root sites are allowed; offsets, couplers, branches and ranges are saved. [Proof and cost scope](../../labs/lab-005-general-h-annealing-relevance/independent/CERTIFIED_EVENT_THEORY.md).

The cost-Lagrange study evaluates375 successful actual candidates from47 compiler models on24 original inputs. Criterion work totals34.67s, median0.608s per pool, excluding prior search and cached standard LP reconstruction. Within balanced compilation,15/23 strictly smaller mappings have actual early-time optimum-event guarantees. All375 actual candidate programs and329 exact selections pass independent audit. [Audit](../../labs/lab-005-general-h-annealing-relevance/results/independent_certified_mapping_audit.json).

[Optimal-set LP](../../labs/lab-005-general-h-annealing-relevance/standard_extension/scripts/optimality_lp.py) only proposes multipliers; exact rational box evaluation validates the bound. Feasible-witness preprocessing is separated into zero-search particular cost and charged bounded descent. It yields1/24 or3/24 standard compact changes, all n16; large cases remain inconclusive. Parent replay checks192 physical root polynomials,960 dual bounds and48 feasible witnesses without an LP/reference solve. [Evidence](../../labs/lab-005-general-h-annealing-relevance/results/independent_standard_extension_audit.json).

Exact rational witnesses use hexadecimal numerator/denominator strings to avoid JSON integer limits. All physical/quantum claims concern the declared ideal model, not a live working graph or QPU. Small exact state/optimum enumeration is reference validation only. Canonical code remains with the lab; [entry points](../../src/README.md) do not maintain duplicate copies.

[Thesis](../thesis.md); [frontier](../ideas/research-frontier.md); [stable takeaway](../../note/general-h-tree-gibbs.md); [source entry points](../../src/README.md).

# General-H readout, finite quantum criteria and a SciCode2 issue

## Findings: outcome and remaining gap

This round develops reusable general-H repair and evaluation algorithms, proves new endpoint and finite-forward statements, and constructs an English standalone [research issue](../../problem/ISSUE-general-h-finite-annealing.md). The issue passes the local creation screen as a plausible research question. It is not yet a calibrated or organizer-approved benchmark.

The strongest new result is an actual ORIGINAL-OPTIMUM probability certificate-guided compact-mapping loop for generalH, in an explicitly early-time quantum regime. Within the balanced compiler, it selects15 strictly smaller mappings on23 ordinary inputs, mean4.075% fewer qubits across all23, while proving higher success probability at common dimensionlessT=1/1024. The basic standard-compiler selector is inconclusive on24/24; a later optimal-set relaxation certifies3/24, all at n16, with charged feasible-search preprocessing. The guaranteed relative gains are tiny, and balanced compilation costs about twice the standard hardware. This is a genuine restricted closed loop, not practical annealer decoding.

## Research question

Can a computationally inexpensive, theoretically justified criterion guide the construction or selection of compact annealer embeddings for general sparse parity-decoding instances, and identify when its choices improve original-error decoding under a common finite forward anneal?

The desired contribution is an algorithm and an honest account of its useful and inconclusive regimes. A globally optimal embedding, a universal winner, a quantum speedup over classical decoders and a simulation of a large commercial QPU are not required. A well-supported negative result is useful if it identifies a consequential limitation and a checkable regime in which a practical decision is possible.

## Mathematical input and decoding target

A decoding instance consists of a sparse binary matrix H with m rows and n columns, a syndrome s in the image of H over GF(2), and finite real additive weights w supplied with an explicit numerical representation. Its target set is

    S* = argmin { w·e : e in {0,1}^n, H e = s mod 2 }.

All tied minimizers count as success. Zero and signed weights are allowed. The score concerns a minimum-cost feasible correction; it is not recovery of a hidden planted error or maximum-likelihood inference of a logical class. No CSS, planar, graphlike, independent-row, bounded-column-degree or named-code assumption may be silently imposed. Sparsity is the main structural information. Code families may illustrate transfer but must not define the entire claim.

Hardware input is an explicit target graph G, individual field/coupling ranges and any coupling-group constraints. An ideal Zephyr graph generated by the public D-Wave graph library is a credential-free reference; deleted sites/couplers may be supplied explicitly. Illustrative numerical ranges must be identified as modelling assumptions rather than a live device profile. Every reduction auxiliary, chain spin, nonzero interaction and physical coefficient must be included.

## Finite-anneal model

For a chosen physical program E(z)=sum_q h_q z_q+sum_(q,r) J_qr z_q z_r on its active physical spins, use

    K(u) = -(1-u) sum_q X_q + u E(Z),
    u=t/T, 0<=t<=T, hbar=1.

Each run starts in |+> on every active physical spin and ends in a computational-basis measurement. All chain and reduction penalties, contact allocations and hardware rescaling are included in E. The driver acts on physical branch spins and auxiliaries. This is an ideal closed-system research model; it is not asserted to describe all commercial-device noise.

The original error is read from the output using a declared deterministic rule fixed before comparing candidates. A root in every original-variable branch is one sufficient convention; another consistently applied rule is allowed if specified and verified. Auxiliary excitations or broken chains do not automatically make the original correction wrong. The primary probability is Pr(e_out in S*), summing every measured state that produces such a correction.

A terminal Gibbs distribution, minimum-energy identity, chain-length statistic, or isolated encoded-state pause comparison does not by itself answer the finite-forward-anneal question. Such results can support a criterion only with their assumptions and transfer limitations made explicit.

## Requested research

Develop a reusable H-to-program procedure and a criterion cheap enough to guide its embedding or programming decisions without repeatedly solving decoding or simulating the entire physical Hilbert space during selection. Explain what the criterion predicts, what it certifies and when it returns inconclusive. Representation, auxiliary construction, routing, contact allocation and the analytic method remain open. Establish the reduction/projection fidelity and physical ground-state conditions, including ties, offsets and scales.
